new_articles.title: Hyundai targets 1 million connected cars by 2027 as software takes over India’s roads
new_articles.summary: Hyundai Motor 관련 기사다. 기사 제목은 'Hyundai targets 1 million connected cars by 2027 as software takes over India’s roads'이다. Hyundai India aims for one million connected car sales by 2027. The automaker is accelerating software-led vehicle technologies across its portfolio. More than 800,000 Hyundai connected cars are already on Indian roads. The Bluelink platform offers over seventy safety and convenience features. Upcoming electric SUVs will feature next-generation connected car technology as standard. The company said on Monday that more than 800,000 Hyundai connected cars are already on Indian roads, with connected vehicle penetration across its portfolio rising five-fold from 4% in 2019 to 20% in 2026 Hyundai said it is also targeting more than two million cumulative connected car sales by 2030 Hyundai said its connected mobility strategy is increasingly centred on software-defined vehicles and over-the-air technology, allowing vehicles to receive software updates and new capabilities after purchase Focus on safety Hyundai said its connected technology has also been used in emergency situations, with Bluelink assisting more than 500,000 motorists through SOS and roadside assistance services Hyundai said its upcoming mass-market electric SUV will offer next-generation connected car technology as standard across all variants, further integrating its connected mobility and electric vehicle strategies.

Reuters FILE PHOTO: A logo of semiconductor and memory chip maker SK Hynix during the company's debut on the Nasdaq market in New York City, U REUTERS/Angelina Katsanis/File Photo A former employee at SK Hynix has been sentenced to 18 months in jail for leaking information on semiconductor manufacturing technology to a Chinese firm, the Yonhap news agency reported ‌on ⁠Sunday The Seoul ⁠High Court made the ruling in an appeal case against the defendant, upholding the lower court's sentence, for leaking classified information on so-called CMOS image sensors , a technology used for non-memory chips in smartphone ⁠cameras and ‌laptops, to a Chinese company in 2022, Yonhap said The court found that ⁠the employee, who formerly worked at SK Hynix's office in China, printed out or took photos of documents containing trade secrets downloaded from the company's internal server, a violation of its security rules, according to Yonhap The defendant disclosed ‌some of the information in a resume submitted to a Chinese firm, ​Yonhap said, ​without naming ⁠the Chinese company. 이 기사는 해당 기업과 연결된 해외 보도를 바탕으로 정리했다.
